Elena (People Ops): Heads-up: new streamlined OKR + self-review flow is live for the upcoming performance cycle. Please review & copy the templates into your team docs: https://redwoodinference.docs/people/okrs-2026
Jordan (People Ops): Quick note 12 there9s now a one-click 'team copy' button in the doc to seed goals. Use it to avoid inconsistent formatting.
Priya (Eng Manager): Awesome. Can you drop a super-short manager checklist here?
Elena (People Ops): Sure 12 manager TL;DR:
- Confirm team has 3 priority OKRs (no more than 5)
- For each OKR, add 1 owner and 1 measurable signal (metric or proxy)
- Mark goals Committed vs Stretch and add milestone dates
- Ask each direct to submit a 1-page self-review + 1 development goal
- Write a 1-2 paragraph manager summary for each direct and suggested rating
people-ops-bot: Reminder: self-reviews open 2026-04-01 09:00 UTC.
Leo (SRE): For infra: many projects span quarters. Any examples for milestones?
Elena (People Ops): Example milestone breakdown for infra OKR:
````
OKR: Reduce inference p99 for hosted API
Q1 milestone: implement batching layer + smoke tests (signal: deploy cadence, unit tests green)
Q2 milestone: KV cache + latency improvement (signal: p50/p99 from canary region)
Metric: p99 latency <= 250ms; Cost per token <= $0.0008
````
Priya (Eng Manager): Thanks. How strict are Committed vs Stretch labels in calibration?
Elena (People Ops): Committed = what they plan to deliver this quarter. Stretch = optional upside. Managers should calibrate in 1:1s and avoid padding committed goals.
Mina (IC): Can I paste a tiny self-review starter I can reuse? I always struggle to be concise.
Jordan (People Ops): Paste this micro-template into your review:
````
What I shipped (2-4 bullets)
Quantified impact (metrics, links to dashboards, demos)
Key challenges and what I learned
Goals for next quarter (incl. 1 dev skill goal)
What I need from my manager (support, unblockers, feedback)
````
Priya (Eng Manager): Do managers need to score via rubric or freeform?
Elena (People Ops): Both: use the rating dropdown (Exceeds/Meets/Needs Improvement) plus a short manager note. Include the date of your calibration 1:1 in the note.
people-ops-bot: Calendar event created 12 "OKR clinic: quick calibration" 2026-03-29 15:00 UTC added to #all-hands.
Leo (SRE): Any sample phrasing for manager notes for cross-functional contributors?
Jordan (People Ops): Try: "Delivered the agreed milestone for Q1 (tracking: link). Collaborated with Product and Runtime to unblock rollout. Suggested rating: Meets. Recommended focus next quarter: increase ownership on reliability area X."
Mina (IC): If someone has a long-running research task that didn't hit milestones, should they be flagged as Needs Improvement?
Elena (People Ops): Not automatically. Document the blockers and updated timeline in the review. Managers should weigh effort vs impact and include that rationale in their note.
Priya (Eng Manager): Perfect 12 I'll run a 15-min OKR primer in our team sync and share the one-page.
Elena (People Ops): Deadlines: self-reviews due 2026-04-10 09:00 UTC; manager reviews due 2026-04-17 17:00 UTC. If you need a different timeline, DM @people-ops with a short justification. :sparkles:
